questions.q:
A swimwear designer has been approached to develop the Australian swimsuit for the Paris Olympic Games in 2024.

What factor should be considered first?
questions.explanation: Function is the primary design factor: a competition swimsuit must first perform its purpose — letting an elite athlete move and swim fast. Aesthetics matters for appeal but is secondary to how well the garment works.

questions.q: What is the most appropriate way a designer could protect the intellectual property of a product such as a smart phone?
questions.explanation: A smartphone is a new functional invention, so its intellectual property is protected by a patent, which covers how a device works. Copyright protects original artistic or written works, not the functional technology of a product.

questions.q:
Four products are categorised according to market demand and manufacturing costs in the table.

|  | Low manufacturing costs | High manufacturing costs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| High market demand | W | X |
| Low market demand | Y | Z |

Which product should generate the most income through sales?
questions.explanation: Product W combines high market demand with low manufacturing costs, so it sells in volume while keeping production costs down — generating the greatest income and profit. X also has high demand but its high manufacturing costs erode the return per sale.

questions.q: Why do designers conduct market research prior to designing a new product?
options: To develop a possible marketing campaign
To determine the level of consumer demand
To understand the impact of a life cycle analysis
questions.explanation: Market research carried out before designing identifies consumer needs and gauges the level of demand, confirming there is a market for the product. A marketing campaign is developed later to sell the product, not the reason research is done up front.

questions.q:
Many Australian homes are currently being designed to bring the indoors to the outdoors.

Which of the following has influenced this practice?
questions.explanation: Blending indoor and outdoor living reflects changing social trends in lifestyle and the way people want to use their homes. Cultural diversity influences design in other ways but is not what drives this particular indoor–outdoor living trend.

questions.q: Which of the following should a designer first consider when conducting an analysis of a targeted audience?
questions.explanation: Analysing a target audience begins with researching market trends — what the audience currently wants and how the market is moving. Purchasing power and cost-to-value are narrower commercial details considered after the broader market direction is understood.

questions.q: Why would a designer make prototypes after creating CAD models for a client?
options: To save time and staff costs
To ensure funding by investors is secured
To demonstrate the final design to the client
To simulate possible issues that may arise in production
questions.explanation: A physical prototype lets the designer test the design in real conditions and simulate problems that could occur in production before committing to manufacture. It is a working test model, not the finished article used to present the final design.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a designer undertaking a 'cradle to grave' analysis of a pending innovation?
options: To determine the likelihood of financial success
To indicate the possibility of future growth in market share
To determine the level of consumer demand for a new product
To understand the impact of the design on society and the environment
questions.explanation: A 'cradle to grave' (life cycle) analysis traces a product from raw materials through use to disposal to reveal its impact on society and the environment. Financial success and market share are commercial aims, not the purpose of this analysis.

questions.q:
A designer is planning to release a line of ergonomic wheelchairs for children.

What is the best way to evaluate the useability of this wheelchair?
options: Test the product in a range of environments
Consider surveys from the specific target market
Compare the design with competitive manufacturers
questions.explanation: Usability is best evaluated by testing the wheelchair in a range of real environments, which directly reveals how well it performs for its users. Surveys gather opinions but do not demonstrate actual usability the way hands-on testing does.

questions.q: The steady increase in the development of innovative and functional consumer goods that quickly become obsolete is mostly the result of
options: demand for newer products with better capabilities.
expansion of online marketing capabilities to increase sales.
use of rapid prototyping methods that produce more products.
advancements in manufacturing methods and the ease of mass production.
questions.explanation: Rapid obsolescence is driven mainly by consumer demand for newer products with improved capabilities, which keeps pushing designers to replace existing goods. Advances in manufacturing make this easier to supply, but the underlying cause is the demand itself.

questions.topic: Research and methods of experimentation to generate ideas
questions.q: Outline how testing and experimenting can improve a design project.

criteria.descriptor: Outlines relevant information regarding testing and experimenting and how it can improve a design

questions.modelAnswer: Testing and experimenting improve a design project by letting the designer explore the successes and failures of different materials, tools and techniques before committing to them. This saves time, money and material wastage and leads to a better-resolved final design.

questions.q: Describe how technology can assist designers in overcoming communication barriers.

criteria.descriptor: Clearly describes how technology assists designers in overcoming communication barriers
Demonstrates an understanding of how technology can be used in overcoming communication barriers

questions.modelAnswer: Clear communication lets designers give and receive definite instructions. Increasingly advanced technologies — online platforms, robotics and automation — are accessible and available to overcome barriers of distance and time, helping designers improve the efficiency, quality and clarity of their communication and collaboration.

questions.topic: Factors affecting designing, appropriateness of design solution, long-term environmental consequences
questions.q:
Two drink bottles are shown: a single-use disposable plastic bottle and a reusable drink bottle.

Discuss the long-term environmental impacts of either drink bottle.

criteria.descriptor: Demonstrates a comprehensive understanding of long-term environmental impacts; provides points for and/or against
Demonstrates a sound understanding of long-term environmental impacts; points for and/or against

questions.modelAnswer: Considering long-term consequences, the reusable bottle is the more appropriate design of the two. Because it can be used many times it produces less waste and less landfill, promotes recycling and represents more responsible marketing and consumer choice. Using biodegradable materials and schemes such as 'return and earn' refunds reinforces this, giving the product lasting value and worth for consumers, society and the environment.

questions.q:
Mass production is the process of creating goods on a large scale and with limited human input.

Explain how the trend towards mass production may affect workplace practices.

criteria.descriptor: Provides a comprehensive explanation of the effects of the mass production trend on workplace practices
Provides an explanation of the effects the mass production trend has on workplace practices
Provides a description of the effects the mass production trend has on workplace practices
Demonstrates some understanding of the effects the mass production trend has on workplace practices

questions.modelAnswer: Mass production reshapes workplace practices in both positive and negative ways. Processes such as robotics, CNC machinery and automation increase the speed and accuracy of producing goods, from injection-moulded plastics to small-batch items, and allow extended hours of operation and total quality management. However, the same trend forces job transition and the upskilling of employees, and can lead to job losses and higher unemployment, affecting individuals' wellbeing and society at large as the nature of work changes with technological advancement.

questions.topic: Impact of design and innovation on society and the environment
questions.q:
The images represent FOUR alternative energy systems: Wind, Solar, Nuclear and Hydrogen.

Analyse the effects of TWO alternative energy systems on society and the environment.

Your answer will be assessed on how well you: demonstrate knowledge and understanding relevant to the question; communicate ideas and information using relevant examples; and present a logical and cohesive response.

criteria.descriptor: Provides an extensive analysis of the effect alternative energy systems have on society and the environment; provides a logical and cohesive response; makes detailed reference to TWO alternative energy systems
Provides some analysis of the effect alternative energy systems have on society and the environment; provides a mostly logical and cohesive response; makes reference to two alternative energy systems
Describes how alternative energy systems have an impact on society and the environment; refers to alternative energy systems
Outlines how alternative energy systems can have an impact on society and the environment
Provides some relevant information about how alternative energy systems can have an impact on society and the environment

questions.modelAnswer: Taking solar and nuclear as the two systems, both can help address climate change but carry significant social and environmental effects. Solar reduces reliance on coal, but the infrastructure must be installed and paid for — favouring higher socioeconomic brackets who can afford the equipment, while lower brackets must spend on basic needs, and the manufacturing of solar panels itself damages the environment. Nuclear can supply large-scale low-emission power and create jobs and upskilling, but it requires a shift in society's views, raises fears of meltdown and the problem of nuclear waste. Both shift the economy — coal exports and fuel-tax revenue fall as fossil-fuel use declines, costing jobs in some sectors while creating new ones, and consumers must be prepared for the additional costs of new equipment. A cohesive analysis weighs these social and environmental trade-offs to judge each system's overall impact.
